skill.name: golang-samber-do
skill.description: Dependency injection in Golang using samber/do — service containers, lifecycle management, scopes, health checks, graceful shutdown, and module organization. Apply when using or adopting samber/do, when the codebase imports github.com/samber/do or github.com/samber/do/v2, or when refactoring manual constructor injection into a DI container.
skill.summary: Build and test Go dependency injection with samber/do v2, including service registration, scopes, lifecycle hooks, and modular containers.
skill.author: samber

content.user_title: Build Go Dependency Injection with samber/do
content.value_statement: Manual service wiring becomes difficult to maintain as Go applications grow. This skill guides samber/do v2 registration, lifecycle management, modular organization, and isolated testing.
actual_capabilities: Guide lazy, transient, named, and pre-created value registration with samber/do v2.
Explain interface-based resolution, provider dependencies, and tagged struct injection.
Organize service registrations into modules with do.Package and child scopes.
Show health check methods, shutdown hooks, signal handling, and shutdown deadlines.
Describe container cloning and mock overrides for isolated service tests.
Demonstrate service listing and injector inspection for dependency debugging.
limitations: Guidance targets samber/do v2; v1 APIs require separate documentation.
Examples are illustrative and require application types, imports, and constructors.
The skill provides guidance, not a bundled application or automated migration tool.
Compilation, test execution, and external documentation access depend on tools available in your environment.

use_cases.title: Replace manual service wiring
use_cases.description: Move application construction into modular samber/do registrations while keeping business logic independent of the container.

use_cases.title: Manage service lifecycles
use_cases.description: Plan shared and request-scoped dependencies, health checks, and shutdown deadlines for a Go service.

use_cases.title: Isolate dependency tests
use_cases.description: Reuse container configuration with clones and mock overrides to test services without production dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first container
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a minimal samber/do v2 container for a Go application. Register configuration and one service, then resolve the service with error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Organize application modules
prompt_templates.prompt: Organize my database, repository, service, and HTTP handler registrations with do.Package. Keep container access at the composition root and inject dependencies through constructors.

prompt_templates.title: Test with dependency overrides
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a samber/do v2 test for my UserService. Clone the application container, override its database dependency with a mock, and explain isolation requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: replace external dependencies in tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review scopes and lifecycle
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my samber/do v2 setup for request isolation, provider failures, health checks, and bounded shutdown. Propose changes and tests against my installed version.

output_examples.input: How should I organize database, cache, and domain service registrations?
output: Group database and cache registrations in an infrastructure package.
Place domain service providers in a separate service package.
Combine registration packages at application startup and pass resolved dependencies to application constructors.

output_examples.input: How can I test a service with a mock database?
output: Clone the application container for the test.
Override the database registration with a compatible mock before resolving the service.
Resolve the service from the test container and assert its behavior.

output_examples.input: How should database connections close during shutdown?
output: Implement a shutdown method on the database service that closes its connection.
Use container shutdown with a timeout context.
Review shutdown errors and verify cleanup with tests.

best_practices: Keep container access in composition and provider code; give business services explicit dependencies.
Match dependency lifetimes to application lifecycles and isolate request-specific state.
Verify examples against your installed v2 release and test provider failures, overrides, and shutdown behavior.
anti_patterns: Pass the injector through business logic as a service locator.
Store request-specific dependencies in the shared root container.
Copy illustrative snippets without adapting types, imports, error handling, and lifecycle cleanup.

faq.question: Which samber/do version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets samber/do v2 and uses the github.com/samber/do/v2 import path.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The declared supported tools are Codex and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does this skill include a runnable application?
faq.answer: No. It includes instructions, illustrative examples, reference guides, and evaluation prompts.

faq.question: Can it help migrate manual constructor wiring?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows migration patterns using providers, registration packages, and resolution at the composition root.

faq.question: How does it support testing?
faq.answer: The testing reference demonstrates container cloning, dependency overrides, mocks, and reusable container setup helpers.

faq.question: Does it cover health checks and shutdown?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains health check methods, shutdown interfaces, signal-based shutdown, and timeout contexts.
